extraction.name: ChartQA
extraction.description: A large-scale benchmark for chart question answering covering 9.6K human-written questions and 23.1K questions generated from human-written chart summaries, focusing on complex reasoning questions involving logical and arithmetic operations over 20,882 real-world charts.
extraction.creator: Ahmed Masry, Do Xuan Long, Jia Qing Tan, Shafiq Joty, Enamul Hoque
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Charts were crawled from four different online sources: Statista, Pew Research, Our World In Data (OWID), and OECD. Human-authored QA pairs were collected using Amazon Mechanical Turk where crowdworkers provided compositional and visual questions with answers. Machine-generated questions were created by fine-tuning a T5 model on human-written chart summaries from Statista.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Manual Human Curator, Software Collection
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Charts (images, SVG files), underlying data tables, metadata (title, chart type), text descriptions, and bounding boxes information of chart elements extracted from SVG files. For Pew dataset, only chart images were available without underlying data tables.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Amazon Mechanical Turk workers were asked to create two types of questions per chart: compositional questions (containing at least two mathematical/logical operations) and visual questions (referring to visual attributes of graphical marks). Each chart received two questions with answers from one worker, then the same questions were answered by another annotator. If answers matched exactly, they were considered correct; otherwise, answers were manually checked to select the final correct answer.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Agreement between crowd workers based on exact matches was 61.04%. Manual checking of 500 random samples found agreement to be 78.55% when considering typos and lexical variations. For machine-generated questions, manual analysis of 1,250 QA pairs found 86.64% were complete, answerable, and correct. The test set of machine-generated dataset was manually cleaned by removing invalid questions.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 2 annotations per question (one worker creates question and answer, another worker answers the same question)
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: T5 model fine-tuned on SQuAD dataset for answer extraction and question generation from human-written chart summaries. ChartOCR model for extracting data tables from chart images.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset has limitations in question generation quality, with some automatically generated questions being incomplete or not answerable from the chart. After filtering, 86.64% of machine-generated questions were found to be complete, answerable, and correct. The dataset also exhibits informal language and typos in questions.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset covers topics including politics, economy, health, society, demographic trends, and public opinion. Politics is a common topic, particularly U.S. Politics & Policy which comprises 45.4% of charts in the Pew dataset.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is designed for training, validation, and testing of Chart Question Answering systems that involve visual and logical reasoning over charts. It is split into training (7,398 human-written questions and 20,901 machine-generated questions), validation (960 questions each), and test sets (1,250 questions each).
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Charts were crawled from four different sources (Statista, Pew research, OWID, OECD). For Pew dataset, only chart images were extracted. For the other three sources, underlying data tables, metadata (title, chart type), SVG files and associated text descriptions were extracted. Bounding boxes information of different chart elements (e.g., x-axis labels) were extracted from SVG files to train data extraction models.
